summary: M1 cursor ratchet: ignore /.cursor/probes/*/target/, born-track extra .cursor receipts/probe sources plus scripts/cursor, and add a reviewed hub-aware GJC transport-guard plugin (policy + constrained tool_call hooks + 8-probe runner + deterministic BUNDLE-HASH).
redBaseline: run-probes.mjs --examined-zero prints examined=0 and exits 1 (fail-closed). Mechanical git add .cursor without the probes-target ignore would stage ~287 MiB under .cursor/probes/wo-residual11-sibling-comment/target/**; git check-ignore -v after the ignore proves the rule bites that tree.
verification: node --test scripts/cursor/gjc-transport-guard/acceptance.mjs 9/9 pass; node scripts/cursor/gjc-transport-guard/run-probes.mjs prints examined=8 and exits 0; node scripts/cursor/gjc-transport-guard/run-probes.mjs --examined-zero exits 1; gjc plugin install scripts/cursor/gjc-transport-guard --user --dry-run --json status=installed; staged tree 1.18 MiB with zero /target/ paths; node scripts/console/validate-lane-receipt.mjs on this receipt exits 0.
commandsRun: git commit -S -m chore(cursor): track process doctrine + hub-aware GJC transport guard
enforcementPlacement: WHERE: the guard runs as a GJC constrained plugin hook on the tool_call event (phase=before, targets bash|edit|write) at session runtime; the subject is the tool call itself, which exists at that point. FINEST DISTINCTION: per-command argv / file payload plus cwd hub path prefix against one shared policy (console vs oyatie grammars). EXAMINED-ZERO FAILS: run-probes.mjs and policy.mjs --examined-zero / --self-report exit 1 when examined==0; the acceptance runner also errors if examined!=8.
peripheralsUpdated: docs/program/console-development-pipeline.md describes the born-tracked cursor ratchet, deny/allow grammar, install command, BUNDLE-HASH registry, and quarantine-on-mismatch; docs/documentation-manifest.seed.json + docs/documentation-index.json regenerated via node scripts/console/generate-documentation-manifest.mjs --write so the pipeline blob_sha matches the index tree.

classification.notes: Process/tooling only. No backend, product, contract, migration, HR, or payroll surface.

preMortem: Risk 1: tracking .cursor/** without a probes-target ignore imports ~287 MiB of Cargo artifacts — mitigated by exact /.cursor/probes/*/target/ and check-ignore evidence. Risk 2: a hook-only spelling that never examines a call goes green — mitigated by fail-closed examined=0. Risk 3: user-scope install from a lane mutates the operator machine — dry-run only. Risk 4: plugin dry-run succeeds but policy.mjs is missing from the copied bundle — policy.mjs is a declared subskill-scoped tool so compile copies it.
blastRadius: Additive under .gitignore, .cursor/** extras, scripts/cursor/gjc-transport-guard/**, and the historical pipeline doc plus regenerated manifests. Does not move or re-home scripts/console/validate-lane-receipt.mjs. Does not install the plugin at user scope.
detection: git check-ignore -v on a probe target path; run-probes examined=8; examined-zero exit 1; gjc plugin install --user --dry-run; tracked validator on this receipt.
rollback: Revert the lane tip commit(s). No hosted state, no user-scope plugin install, no data coupling.
stopConditions: Validator nonzero; staged target/ tree; plugin dry-run failure; probe runner examined!=8.
followUps: Integration owner: open/merge the console PR, restack if origin/main moves, and perform any real (non-dry-run) plugin install at the chosen scope.
Do not install this bundle at user scope from a lane; dry-run only was executed.
challenges: Chesterton: mechanical git add .cursor/** would add ~291MB of Cargo build artifacts under .cursor/probes/wo-residual11-sibling-comment/target/** (observed 287 MiB on disk). That is indefensible as doctrine tracking. Resolved in the same PR by the exact ignore /.cursor/probes/*/target/, proven by git check-ignore -v .cursor/probes/wo-residual11-sibling-comment/target/debug and a staged tree of 1.18 MiB with zero /target/ paths.
A hook that only inspects bash command strings would miss -fast slugs and foreign-transport text written via edit/write; the guard therefore examines bash, edit, and write payloads.
